identity.name: Azure AD Sync Module Load via Suspicious Process Injection
identity.summary: An attacker loads a malicious Azure AD sync module via process injection to gain persistence and execute commands. Cortex should detect the unusual module load behavior and process injection.
identity.description: An attacker loads a malicious Azure AD sync module via process injection to gain persistence and execute commands. Cortex should detect the unusual module load behavior and process injection.

techniques.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder

payload.code:
powershell.exe -WindowStyle Hidden -Command "[System.Reflection.Assembly]::Load([System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes('C:\\temp\\syncmodule.dll'))"

rundll32.exe C:\\temp\\syncmodule.dll,EntryPoint

netstat -an | findstr 192.0.2.1

manual_steps: Not authored. Write and test cleanup before promotion.

biocs.name: Unusual Azure AD Sync Module Load
biocs.description: Detection of unexpected module loading into a process during Azure AD sync behavior
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = 'rundll32.exe'
| filter action_file_path contains 'syncmodule.dll'
